newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures end sharply up on cash bond buying.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures end sharply up on cash bond buying.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended sharply higher on Monday, boosted by strong demand for cash bonds in the afternoon.
"Investors were detected buying cash JGBs, primarily in the long-term zone," said a brokerage trader.
Public funds were detected buying JGB issues between the benchmark 182nd bond and the 188th issue, the trader said.
Traders also said a rise in U.S. Treasury bonds after the release of U.S. employment data last Friday helped support JGBs.
The December ended at 121.34, up from Friday's 120.64.
Turnover in the December was was 71,308 contracts.
"Traders were influenced not so much by the figures in the U.S. employment report, but by the subsequent movements in U.S. Treasury bonds," said a trader for another securities firm.
The trader added, however, that this was not enough to fully explain the sudden rise of the December futures contract.

"I can't remember a key JGB futures contract rising by as much as 70 basis points in one day, as it did today, without any concrete factors such as economic indicators or comments by politicians and the like," he said.
"The traders I've talked to all said they're spooked by the December's rise," the trader added.

In the morning, the December futures rose as dealers covered short positions made before the release of the U.S. employment report. Cash JGBs were relatively quiet and investors were inactive during morning trade, dealers said.
"Morning trade concentrated by far on the key futures contract, while cash bond buying picked up in the afternoon," the second trader said.
The cash benchmark 182nd JGBs were yielding 2.920 percent, down from Friday's 2.990 percent, as of 0653 GMT.
Traders said they did not expect the Japan July machinery orders data, due on Tuesday, to have much effect on JGBs unless they deviate greatly from market expectations.
"Machinery orders data have a tendency to fluctuate anyway, so I don't think the data will have much effect on the JGB market," said a city bank trader.
The trader said he expects July machinery orders to have risen by one percent from the previous month.
"Unless the data is much stronger than expected, I don't think there will be much effect on JGBs," a trust bank trader said. -- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-5473-3748)
